company: Deloitte India (Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP / Deloitte South Asia LLP / Deloitte Shared Services India LLP) + Deloitte USI
company_verdict:
Blunt version: the Deloitte job portal is the wrong door for him, and the research proves it rather than guesses it. Both live boards (2,031 India-board postings + 714 USI postings = 2,745) are experienced-hire boards. Zero postings mention a 2027 start, a deferred joining date, or a final-semester internship. The only two interns on the entire India board are in Colombo, Sri Lanka. The only "Management Trainee" req with a 0-2 year band (57942344, Bhubaneswar) is a PySpark data-engineering seat, and Spark is on his hard no-list. One of the best content-fit reqs (59268144) says "Immediate joiners preferred" in the qualification block.

Mumbai is worse than the headline number suggests. Of 277 Mumbai postings, the overwhelming majority are SAP/Oracle ERP, Cyber (Data Privacy / TPRM / SOC), Tax, Audit, or Assistant Manager-and-above. Mumbai analytics titles are repeatedly gated behind an accounting qualification — req 110426 says "Education - ACCA Affiliate or ACCA Member"; the Mumbai External Audit Analyst req demands "B.Com/M.Com from a NAAC 'A' Graded Campus". Genuinely reachable Mumbai openings for a May-2027 B.Tech: TWO (reqs 110231 and 110382), plus one multi-city Power BI req (110508) that lists Mumbai as an eligible location. That is the honest count.

Roles I deliberately EXCLUDED and why, so he does not waste applications: 59070444 Enabling Areas IT AM BI Developer Mumbai — "Minimum of 3-5 years"; 58524244 Executive Financial Risk Mumbai — "3 to 5 years"; 60040244 Analyst Financial Spreading Delhi — "2-6 Years of experience in corporate credit analysis" plus CA/CFA/FRM preferred; 58605244 Consultant Audit ITDA Mumbai — hard gate "Education - ACCA Affiliate or ACCA Member"; 59668844 Cyber CST Consultant Mumbai — "2-4 years of experience Third-Party Risk Management"; 59619444 National Office Analyst Delhi — asks B.Com/BBA/CA(Inter) AND a Master's in Finance/Business/Economics, which a B.Tech CSE is not; 58007344 Senior Consultant NAT:Operations Corporate Strategy — "2-8 years", the single best CONTENT fit on the board for his case-competition and market-research profile, and the role he should target in 2028, not 2026; 57942344 Management Trainee Risk Tech Bhubaneswar — PySpark; 60054644 Analyst Financial Services Finance Transformation — written gate is open ("Any Graduate", no years) but the real gate is IFRS/local GAAP statement preparation and subledger/GL reconciliation, which he has zero of; 57779544 — CA/MBA-gated. All three USI analyst/research roles I checked (367687, 352771, 366994) require a Master's, and USI has ZERO Mumbai-primary roles.

Net: Deloitte India is worth real effort for him, but almost none of that effort belongs in the online application form. It belongs in the DJSCE placement cell and in referral conversations.
best_channel:
1) DJSCE Training & Placement Office, this week. Deloitte recruits India via campus and Deloitte USI's own students page says only "get in touch with your campus placement team". Collegedunia lists Deloitte among DJSCE recruiters (third-party, unverified by Deloitte) — the TPO is the authority. Two questions to ask them: (a) does Deloitte hold a slot in the 2027 season, and (b) is that slot Deloitte India (Mumbai consulting/risk/T&T) or Deloitte USI (Hyderabad/Bengaluru delivery)? That distinction decides everything for him — USI is Hyderabad-centric with no Mumbai-primary roles.

2) NLA (National Level Assessment) — Deloitte India's off-campus fresher drive for Analyst Trainee / Associate Analyst. UNVERIFIED on any deloitte.com domain; the 2026-batch close date of 19 Jan 2026, the Rs 3.25-4.0 LPA band and the 1-year apprenticeship probation all come from aggregator blogs (offcampusjobs4u, freshersnow, careerwithmohit). Do NOT repeat those numbers as fact. But if the cycle repeats, a 2027-batch NLA plausibly opens Dec 2026-Jan 2027, which lands exactly in his window. Set a weekly calendar check from 1 Dec 2026 on southasiacareers.deloitte.com plus Deloitte India's LinkedIn careers page. This is the single highest-value thing for him to watch.

3) Referral into req 112515 (Analyst | Risk Management | Bengaluru, Cyber Strategy & Transformation). It is the ONLY posting across 2,745 that explicitly counts internships and academic projects as qualifying experience. A referral here is the highest-yield individual action available.

4) Portal applications: worth doing for the seven no-years-stated Analyst-grade reqs below, but treat them as lottery tickets with a referral multiplier, not as a plan.

Note for whoever chases links: Deloitte's own India careers page still links to jobsindia.deloitte.com, which is NXDOMAIN and dead. careersindia.deloitte.com is also dead. The working portal is southasiacareers.deloitte.com.
may_2027_fit:
Poor on the portal, decent through campus. Across 2,745 live postings on both Deloitte portals, not one mentions a 2027 start, a deferred joining date, a graduate programme, or a final-semester internship. There is currently NO posted Deloitte India route to a Jan-May 2027 internship — such an arrangement would have to be created by a referral or by the DJSCE placement cell, not applied for.

What he should declare on every application and in every referral conversation, verbatim and up front, never buried: "B.Tech CSE (Data Science), DJSCE Mumbai, graduating May 2027. Available full-time from June 2027. Available full-time on-site for a final-semester internship from January 2027 through May 2027." Putting it in the first two lines of the cover note filters him out of reqs he was never going to get and makes him the obvious candidate for the ones where a team is planning ahead. Hiding it wastes his time and burns referrals.

Hard exclusion on timing: req 111719 (Analyst | S&T - Advanced Analytics) states "Immediate joiners preferred" in the qualification block. That is the best content match on the board for him and it is currently closed by his graduation date. Track the team, re-approach Feb-Mar 2027.

picks.title: Analyst | Risk Management | Bengaluru | Cyber Strategy & Transformation
picks.location: Bengaluru, IN — Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP
picks.eligible: YES — and it is the only unambiguous YES on either portal. The experience line reads "0-2 years of relevant experience, including internships or academic", which explicitly admits his profile rather than tolerating it.
picks.years_bar: 0-2 years, internships and academic work explicitly counted. The single most open experience gate across all 2,745 postings.
picks.why_fit: Posted "0-2 years of relevant experience, including internships or academic" vs his ~13 months across CypherSOL, Sereno Volante, Bigul and Infiheal — counted as written, not argued. Posted "Proficiency in Python and SQL" vs Python (strong) and SQL (strong). Posted duty "Assist in preparing security reports, dashboards, presentations, and compliance documentation using tools such as Excel and data analysis libraries" vs the CypherSOL pipelines that turned multi-format bank statements into model-ready data with pandas, plus the Infiheal Series A deck he owned end-to-end. Posted duty "Leverage Python and automation to improve cybersecurity processes and reduce manual effort" vs the CypherSOL ML work that replaced rule-based transaction-category and entity-recognition analytics. Posted good-to-have "Knowledge of AWS Machine Learning services such as SageMaker, Rekognition, or Comprehend" vs AWS Academy ML Foundations. Posted good-to-have "Experience with Pandas, PostgreSQL, Excel, or data analysis" vs pandas/NumPy/scikit-learn. Posted good-to-have "Internship, academic project, or hands-on experience in ... software development" vs LawzyAI (FastAPI + sklearn + React, live) and KOP AI. Posted "B.E./B.Tech in Computer Engineering, Computer Science ... or a related discipline" vs B.Tech CSE, CGPA 8.82, no backlogs.
picks.gaps: Zero cybersecurity domain exposure: no ISO 27001, no NIST CSF, no GRC, no SOC operations, no IAM, no BCP/DR — five named requirement bullets he currently cannot evidence at all. No cybersecurity certification of any kind. AWS beyond an Academy intro cert is not real cloud experience and he should not claim it is. Bengaluru, not Mumbai — he needs to be willing to relocate or this is moot.
picks.learnable_edge: Two items, both inside his 2-6 week window, both clearing a named bullet. (1) ISO 27001:2022 Foundation plus a read-through of NIST CSF 2.0 (free from NIST) — 2-3 weeks — clears "Familiarity with ISO 27001 and NIST cybersecurity frameworks" and moves "Knowledge of GRC, Risk Management, SOC Operations, IAM, and BCP/DR" from nothing to the "basic understanding" the req actually asks for. (2) AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner — 3 weeks — clears "Basic understanding of cloud computing and AWS" with a credential instead of a claim. Do NOT attempt a deep security cert; the bar here is literally "basic" and "familiarity".
picks.referral_leverage: HIGHEST of any role listed — this is where he should spend his single best referral. Because the written gate already admits him, a referral is not being asked to bend a rule, only to get the CV read. Approach in order: (a) DJSCE alumni on LinkedIn filtered to Deloitte India, Bengaluru, Cyber / Risk Advisory — ask specifically for requisition 112515 by number; (b) anyone in Deloitte India Cyber Strategy & Transformation, which is a large Bengaluru and Mumbai practice; (c) Deloitte often sponsors and judges campus case competitions — his 4th-of-400+ at Ace The Case IIT Bombay and the IIM Ahmedabad Innovability finish are legitimate openers to a Deloitte consultant who judged or attended.
picks.timing: Apply now, this week. Declare: "Graduating May 2027, available June 2027 full-time, available on-site January-May 2027 for a final-semester internship." Even if they fill it before June 2027, the 0-2 year band means this team hires at his grade repeatedly — being a known name when the next 112515-equivalent opens is worth the application on its own.

picks.title: Technology & Transformation - Data Analyst | Bengaluru | Engineering | Data Modernization & Migration
picks.job_id: 58184444 (no requisition ID printed on the page)
picks.location: Filed under Hyderabad, IN; the title says Bengaluru — clarify with the recruiter, it is a real ambiguity
picks.eligible: YES as written. No experience band appears anywhere in the posting; the only stated education gate is "Graduation - B./B.tech", which he clears. Analyst grade.
picks.years_bar: NOT STATED. No years anywhere in the posting. Grade (Analyst) is the only signal, and Analyst is the entry rung of the Deloitte India ladder.
picks.why_fit: This is the cleanest pure data-analyst JD on the board and it is the job he says he wants. Posted "Proficiency in SQL for data extraction and manipulation is required" vs SQL (strong). Posted "analytical programming skills in Python (Pandas, NumPy) or R for advanced data analysis and modeling" vs Python (strong), pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn — the CypherSOL transaction-categorisation and entity-recognition models are the direct evidence. Posted "Proficiency with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Looker) for dashboard creation and reporting" — the bullet is satisfied as written by Power BI, which he has; the "e.g." makes Tableau optional, not required. Posted "Exceptional analytical and quantitative skills, with the ability to collect, organize, analyze, and disseminate significant amounts of information" vs the freelance registration platform that handled 10,000+ users in 8 days with funnel drop-off tracking. Posted "Strong problem-solving abilities, capable of tackling complex business challenges with a data-driven approach" vs 4th of 400+ at Ace The Case IIT Bombay, Spotify case win at KJ Somaiya, Analytrix'26 Datathon win.
picks.gaps: Posted "Experience with CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce) and understanding of sales data structures" — he has none, and this is one of four technical bullets, so it is a quarter of the technical gate. No Tableau and no Looker if a screener reads the bullet strictly rather than as written. No data-migration or data-modernization project experience, which is the practice's actual subject matter.
picks.learnable_edge: Salesforce Trailhead "Data Modeling" plus "Sales Cloud Basics" trails — 1-2 weeks, free, and produces badges he can cite — directly addresses "Experience with CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce) and understanding of sales data structures", the only bullet he currently fails. Tableau Desktop Specialist — 3 weeks — converts the visualization bullet from "satisfied as written" to "satisfied on every listed tool". Both are squarely inside his window and neither touches Java or C++.
picks.referral_leverage: HIGH. "No years stated" is exactly the situation where a referral decides the outcome — with no number in the req, the screener falls back on grade convention and CV pedigree, and a referral overrides that. Target DJSCE alumni in Deloitte India T&T Engineering (Bengaluru or Hyderabad). Ask the referrer to confirm the actual base location before he applies, because the Hyderabad-filed / Bengaluru-titled mismatch is unresolved and it changes whether he can even take the role.
picks.timing: Apply now. State the May 2027 graduation in the first two lines. If the team says it needs someone sooner, pivot the conversation immediately to the Jan-May 2027 final-semester internship — a data-migration engagement with a defined workstream is exactly the kind of work a five-month intern can be given, and he should propose it explicitly rather than wait to be offered it.

picks.title: Enabling Areas - DEC - Senior Executive - Data Science - Bengaluru
picks.location: Bengaluru, IN — Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP
picks.eligible: YES on the written bar — this posting has no years band AND no education requirement at all, which is the least-gated req on the entire board. "Senior Executive" is a mid-junior Deloitte India grade, above fresher, so the unwritten bar is real.
picks.years_bar: NOT STATED, and unusually no degree line either. Grade (Senior Executive) is the only bar and it sits above pure-fresher.
picks.why_fit: Posted "Ability to perform exploratory data analysis to discover interesting trends and relationships" vs EDA on his stated skill list and the CypherSOL bank-statement work. Posted "Experience applying statistical modelling, machine learning, NLP, and other quantitative techniques to solve business problems" vs scikit-learn, NLP, and the CypherSOL entity-recognition and transaction-category models that replaced rule-based analytics — that is a business problem solved with ML, stated as such. Posted preferred "Any exposure to Generative AI would be a great addition" vs LawzyAI (IPC/BNS legal RAG, FastAPI + sklearn + React, live) and KOP AI (10 parallel stateful LLM agents, 60-90s cut to 8-12s, RAG with page and timestamp citations) — that is far past "any exposure" and is the strongest single differentiator he has for this req. Posted "Possess understanding of and ability to communicate statistics to experts and non-experts" vs the Infiheal Series A investor narrative he owned end-to-end. Posted duty "Build, execute, and evaluate A/B tests" vs the freelance funnel drop-off tracking and WhatsApp/SMS re-engagement work.
picks.gaps: Posted "Experience in deep learning" — a real gap he must not oversell. His ONNX FER work in LearnSphere is inference-side deployment of an existing model plus a per-user SVM on top; it is not training deep networks. If asked, say that plainly. Also: this is internal product and platform data science for Deloitte India's Digital Excellence Centre, not client-facing consulting, so it is a partial fit against his stated want for strategy and consulting exposure.
picks.learnable_edge: A short, genuine deep-learning artefact — fine-tune one transformer on a real dataset and ship it, 3-4 weeks with PyTorch or Hugging Face on free Colab — converts "Experience in deep learning" from a fail to a defensible claim. This is the only gap on this posting, so the effort maps to a single bullet with a clean payoff. Nothing else here needs learning; he already over-satisfies the GenAI preference.
picks.referral_leverage: MEDIUM-HIGH. With no years and no degree line written, the screen is entirely discretionary, which cuts both ways — a referral is close to decisive, and its absence means an automated sift on grade convention. Target the Deloitte India Digital Excellence Centre (DEC) in Bengaluru specifically; it is an internal-capability group, smaller and less trafficked than the client practices, so a warm intro carries further there than it would into Cyber or T&T.
picks.timing: Apply now, but rank it third. Internal capability teams in Deloitte India plan headcount on a longer horizon than client-serving practices, which makes a June 2027 start easier for them to absorb than for a staffed-to-project team. Say so explicitly when he applies — frame the May 2027 date as something they can plan around rather than an obstacle.

picks.title: T&T - EAID - Platform Development & Integration - Analyst | Generative AI | Bengaluru | Engineering
picks.location: Bengaluru, IN — Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP
picks.eligible: YES on the written gate — no years band, and the education line "Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field" is cleared by B.Tech CSE. Analyst grade.
picks.years_bar: NOT STATED. No experience band in the posting at all. Analyst grade.
picks.why_fit: Posted "Programming & Data Analytics: Proficiency in Python and SQL for automation and data analysis" vs Python (strong) and SQL (strong). Posted duty "Security Automation & Analytics: Utilize programming tools (Python, SQL) to automate reporting workflows and build data-driven dashboards to monitor security and business performance" vs the CypherSOL automation pipelines plus Power BI — this is his actual job description with the word "security" inserted. Posted duty "AI & Emerging Tech Security: Assist in evaluating the security of AI implementations, focusing on Responsible AI" vs KOP AI's 10 parallel stateful LLM agents and LawzyAI's RAG with page and timestamp citations — citation-grounded retrieval is a Responsible AI control and he has built one, which almost no other Analyst applicant will have. Posted duty "Reporting & Documentation: Contribute to the drafting of high-level industry reports" vs the Infiheal Series A deck and narrative he owned end-to-end. Posted education "Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field" vs B.Tech CSE Data Science, CGPA 8.82.
picks.gaps: Named and unmet: NIST CSF 2.0, COBIT, ISO 27001, PCI DSS — four frameworks, zero exposure. "Strong understanding of Information Security, Cloud Security, Digital Trust, and Third-Party Risk Management" — he has none of these four domains. "Basic understanding of cryptographic concepts (e.g., AES, RSA, hashing, and digital signatures)" — undergraduate-level and recoverable, but currently unevidenced. Certification line: he holds no ISC2 CC or equivalent.
picks.learnable_edge: ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC) — the self-paced course and the exam are free under ISC2's One Million Certified in Cybersecurity programme, and it takes 2-3 weeks. The posting says "Possession of (or progress toward) ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC) or similar industry certifications", so even enrolling satisfies the bullet, and passing it converts the single named certification requirement into a checked box for zero rupees. The CC syllabus also covers cryptography basics and security principles, so one 3-week effort clears the cert line AND the cryptography line. Add a NIST CSF 2.0 read-through (free, one week) for the frameworks bullet.
picks.referral_leverage: MEDIUM-HIGH. Title says Generative AI and the body is digital-risk GRC — that mismatch means the applicant pool is probably full of ML engineers who will fail the GRC bullets and GRC people who will fail the Python bullets. He can credibly do both halves once the CC cert is in hand, and a referrer can make exactly that argument. Target DJSCE alumni in Deloitte India T&T EAID, Bengaluru.
picks.timing: Get the ISC2 CC first — it is 2-3 weeks and free, and it upgrades this application and the Mumbai governance role (110231) and the Cyber Risk role (112515) simultaneously. Apply by late October 2026. Declare June 2027 availability and offer the Jan-May 2027 internship.

picks.title: T&T | EAID | Engineering | Power BI | Consultant / Senior Consultant / Manager | Multiple Location
picks.location: Filed under Bengaluru, IN; the posting states "Location - Mumbai, Pune, Coimbatore, BBSR, Chennai, Hyderabad, Delhi" — the only BI req on the board that lists Mumbai
picks.eligible: Yes on the written gate, no on the unwritten one. The posting states no years and asks only "Education - B. tech or BE". But the grade band opens at Consultant, and Consultant at Deloitte India conventionally means 2-4 years. Treat the silence on years as an omission, not an invitation.
picks.years_bar: NOT STATED. Grade band "Consultant / Senior Consultant / Manager" — Consultant is the entry point being hired against and is roughly two grades above where a May-2027 graduate enters.
picks.why_fit: Posted "Developing visual reports, dashboards and KPI scorecards using Power BI desktop" vs Power BI on his stated stack. Posted "Connecting to data sources, importing data and transforming data for Business Intelligence" vs the CypherSOL pipelines that ingested multi-format bank statements and produced model-ready data — that is source connection and transformation, in production, at a fintech. Posted "Excellent in analytical thinking for translating data into informative visuals and reports" vs the Infiheal investor deck and the freelance funnel drop-off dashboards. Posted "Qualifications: Education - B. tech or BE" vs B.Tech CSE. This is the only BI or Power BI requisition on the entire 2,031-posting India board that lists Mumbai as an eligible location AND states no years requirement AND asks only for a B.Tech — that combination does not occur twice.
picks.gaps: Precisely named and currently unmet: DAX ("Proficient in making DAX queries in Power BI desktop"), row-level security ("Able to implement row level security on data and have an understanding of application security layer models in Power BI"), tabular and multidimensional modelling ("Able to develop tabular and multidimensional models that are compatible with warehouse standards"), Analysis Services ("Building Analysis Services reporting models"), and Power BI Service publishing and scheduling. His Power BI is report-building depth, not semantic-model depth. Separately, the grade is the real blocker and no amount of DAX fixes it.
picks.learnable_edge: This is the highest-leverage learning target on the whole list. Microsoft PL-300 (Power BI Data Analyst) — 4-5 weeks — covers DAX, Power Query / M, row-level security, and tabular semantic models, which between them are FOUR of the nine named required skills on this posting. Nothing in PL-300 requires Java, C++, Spark or a warehouse. It also strengthens reqs 58184444, 58386644 and every future Deloitte BI opening, which is why it ranks first in skills_to_learn.
picks.referral_leverage: CRITICAL — without a referral this is not a real application, because the Consultant grade will sift him out before anyone reads the CV. With one, the argument is narrow and winnable: the req states no years, states only a B.Tech, and he will hold PL-300. Target DJSCE alumni in Deloitte India T&T EAID who sit in the Mumbai or Pune office, since those are the two listed locations nearest him. Ask the referrer directly whether the team would consider an Analyst-grade hire against this req, or a Jan-May 2027 intern — that question is more likely to produce a yes than the application itself.
picks.timing: Do PL-300 first (4-5 weeks, so late October 2026), then apply. Applying before the cert wastes the one Mumbai-eligible BI req on the board. When he does apply, lead with Mumbai as his preferred location — he is local, which is a genuine cost advantage to a staffing manager and worth saying out loud.

picks.title: Senior Analyst | Governance and Policy Development | Mumbai | Cyber Strategy & Transformation
picks.location: Mumbai, IN — Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP
picks.eligible: YES. The posting states no years number and self-describes as early-career: "This role is ideal for early-career professionals who are passionate about cloud technologies, security best practices, and governance frameworks." Education gate "Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or a related field" is cleared by B.Tech CSE.
picks.years_bar: NOT STATED as a number; the posting explicitly frames itself as early-career. One of only two genuinely reachable Mumbai openings for him on a 277-posting Mumbai board.
picks.why_fit: Posted "This role is ideal for early-career professionals" — there is no years number to disqualify him, and Deloitte India wrote that sentence deliberately. Posted "Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or a related field" vs B.Tech CSE, CGPA 8.82, no backlogs. Posted "Familiarity with scripting languages such as PowerShell, Python, or Bash is an advantage" vs Python (strong). Posted preferred certification "AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner / Microsoft Azure Fundamentals" — already on his own 2-6 week learn list, so the single named preferred credential is three weeks away. Posted "Good written and verbal communication skills" vs the Infiheal Series A deck and narrative he owned end-to-end and the 13 podium finishes in case competitions. It is in Mumbai, at Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP (the client-facing India practice, not the shared-services back office), which is the combination he actually wants.
picks.gaps: Honest and substantial. Posted "Understanding of networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, Firewalls, VPNs)" — he has TCP socket programming from GitLane but not networking fundamentals as a discipline, and a Deloitte interviewer will find the difference in two questions. Posted "Basic knowledge of Linux and Windows operating systems" — no systems administration background. Posted "Knowledge of cloud security concepts including IAM, networking, encryption, logging, and monitoring" and "Familiarity with cloud governance principles and security frameworks" — no exposure. Bigger point: this is governance, policy and audit-evidence documentation work, not analytics. It is an excellent fit on the GATE and a partial fit on his stated INTEREST. He should only take it if a Mumbai seat at Deloitte India matters more to him than doing analytics, and he should decide that before he interviews, not after.
picks.learnable_edge: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner — 3 weeks, roughly Rs 8,000 — is named in the posting as the preferred certification and simultaneously covers IAM, logging, monitoring and encryption basics, which is the "Knowledge of cloud security concepts" bullet. One cert, two bullets, on a Mumbai role. Add the free Cisco Networking Academy "Introduction to Networks" module (2 weeks) for TCP/IP, DNS, firewalls and VPNs, which is the remaining named gap. Total: 5 weeks to go from partially qualified to fully matching the written requirements of a Mumbai Deloitte India req.
picks.referral_leverage: HIGH, and this is where a Mumbai-based referrer is worth more than a Bengaluru one. DJSCE is in Vile Parle; Deloitte India's Mumbai Cyber practice is large (I counted well over 40 Cyber and Data Privacy postings in Mumbai alone), so the alumni density should be real. Ask the DJSCE TPO and the DJS S4DS alumni network — he was Head of Marketing there, which is a legitimate reason to be in touch with seniors who graduated into consulting.
picks.timing: Do AWS Cloud Practitioner first (3 weeks), then apply in mid-to-late October 2026 with the cert on the CV. An early-career Mumbai req is scarce enough that he should not fire it off uncertified. Declare June 2027 availability and explicitly offer Jan-May 2027 on-site in Mumbai — being local for a five-month final-semester internship is a concrete, cheap proposition for a Mumbai team, and it is the single most plausible route to a Deloitte internship anywhere in this dataset.

picks.title: Analyst | FT: Strategy & Ops | Bengaluru | Finance Transformation | Finance Strategy
picks.location: Bengaluru, IN — Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP
picks.eligible: YES on paper — no years stated and the education line "Educational Qualifications: BE, B. Tech - Undergraduate, M. Tech" explicitly names undergraduate B.Tech. Scored down only because the work is not what he says he wants.
picks.years_bar: NOT STATED. No years band. Analyst grade, undergraduate B.Tech explicitly named.
picks.why_fit: Highest raw skills overlap of any posting on the board, close to line-for-line. Posted "Should have experience in Python, JavaScript/Typescript and SQL" vs Python (strong), JS/TS, SQL (strong). Posted "Hands on experience on React.js, Node.js, FastAPI frameworks" vs LawzyAI, which is FastAPI + scikit-learn + React and is live in production. Posted "Demonstrated technical capability in developing applications using any industry-standard RDBMS/NoSQL Databases" vs ChromaDB and SQL. Posted "Experience in building applications on cloud platforms like AWS/Azure/GCP" vs AWS Academy ML Foundations and Google Cloud GenAI Skills Boost plus Docker. Posted "Sound knowledge on Data Structures, Algorithms, and excellent problem-solving skills" vs B.Tech CSE at 8.82 and the ML Quest Hackathon win. Posted preferred "Proficient in Microsoft Office suite of products such as PowerPoint, Visio, Excel, Word" vs the Infiheal investor deck work.
picks.gaps: The gap is not skills, it is direction. Despite the "Strategy & Ops" title, the stated profile is a full-stack engineering seat — React, Node, FastAPI, unit testing with Jest, Mocha and PyTest, Agile delivery. He explicitly said NOT core SDE. Genuine missing items are minor: no Node.js, no formal unit-testing practice (Jest/Mocha/PyTest), no Visio. Note also the companion req 57779544 in the same Finance Strategy team is CA/MBA-gated ("Candidates CA Qualified- 1st Attempt preferred / MBA from a premium institute / CPA/ACA/ACCA/CIMA/CFA") and is closed to him — so the non-engineering door into this practice is shut.
picks.learnable_edge: PyTest plus one of Jest or Mocha — one week, and he already writes the code they would test — clears "Experience in writing unit test cases using Jest, Mocha and PyTest frameworks", which is the only technical bullet he currently fails outright. But be honest about what the effort buys: it makes him a stronger candidate for a job he said he does not want. Only spend the week if he decides a foot in the Finance Strategy practice is worth two years of engineering work first.
picks.referral_leverage: MEDIUM. He does not need a referral to pass the skills screen here — he genuinely matches it — so a referral adds less than it does on the Power BI or Senior Consultant reqs. Where a referrer IS useful is answering the only question that matters: is this seat actually engineering, or does the Analyst do strategy work with a technical toolkit? Ask before applying. A DJSCE alumnus anywhere in Deloitte India Finance Transformation can answer it in one message.
picks.timing: Fallback only, and a deliberate one. If he wants Deloitte India on the CV more than he wants an analytics first job, this is his easiest written route in, with an internal move to Finance Strategy later. If he does not, skip it — applying to and accepting a role he described as off-limits is how people lose two years. Decide before applying, not at the offer.

picks.title: Analyst | S&T - Advanced Analytics | Bengaluru | Supply Chain & Network Operations
picks.location: Bengaluru, IN — Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP
picks.eligible: NO, for timing reasons only, and the block is explicit. The qualification block contains exactly four lines and one of them is "Immediate joiners preferred". He cannot start before June 2027. On content this would score in the low 80s; the date is what kills it.
picks.years_bar: "1-3 Years experience" — his ~13 months of internships is a defensible read of the bottom of that band. The years are not the problem.
picks.why_fit: On content this is the best strategy-analytics match on the board. Posted duty "Understand client business issues and translate them into analytics/data science problems" vs CypherSOL, where he replaced rule-based transaction analytics with ML models for category and entity recognition — a business problem translated into a data science problem, shipped. Posted duty "Work with Partners and Directors to develop pursuit responses and build impactful presentations" vs Infiheal, where he owned the Series A investor deck and narrative end-to-end and contributed to closing co-investors, plus the IndiGo and HDFC Bank B2B pipeline taken to proposal stage — that IS pursuit work. Posted duty "Manage projects and programs using state of the art AI and Generative AI capabilities" vs KOP AI (10 parallel stateful LLM agents, latency cut from 60-90s to 8-12s) and LawzyAI. Posted duty "High level knowledge of data science and AI systems to translate business issues into data science solutions and solutions into insights stories" vs 4th of 400+ at Ace The Case IIT Bombay and the Analytrix'26 Datathon win. Posted education "Any Graduate" — the loosest education gate on the board.
picks.gaps: No supply chain or network operations domain exposure whatsoever — his fintech, algo-trading, mental-health and legal-tech background touches none of it. No full-time consulting delivery experience. But the operative gap is not a skill: it is that the posting wants someone who can start now and he cannot until June 2027.
picks.learnable_edge: Nothing here is worth learning to fix the timing, because timing is not learnable. If he wants to be ready when this team reopens a req in 2027, the useful 3-4 week investment is supply-chain analytics fundamentals — demand forecasting, inventory optimisation, network design — via a short course, plus one portfolio project doing demand forecasting on a public retail dataset with the pandas and scikit-learn he already has. That closes the only real skills gap on an otherwise excellent match.
picks.referral_leverage: MEDIUM now, HIGH in early 2027. The only referral conversation worth having today is a narrow one: "can a mid-2027 start be accommodated on this team, and do you take final-semester interns January to May?" If the answer is no, thank them and diarise. Do not spend a strong referral pushing a candidate against an explicit "Immediate joiners preferred" line — that burns the contact for nothing.
picks.timing: Do NOT apply now. Track the team and re-apply February-March 2027 for a June 2027 start, or approach in October 2026 specifically to ask about a Jan-May 2027 internship. This is the clearest case on the whole list of a role he will be right for at the wrong moment, and the correct move is patience plus a calendar entry, not an application.

picks.title: Senior Consultant | Project Management | Bengaluru | Artificial Intelligence & Data | AI Insights & Engagement
picks.job_id: 59240244 (no requisition ID printed on the page)
picks.eligible: Written gate: YES ("Education: Any Graduate", no years stated). Real gate: NO — Senior Consultant at Deloitte India conventionally means 4+ years and he will have zero full-time. Referral-only shot.
picks.years_bar: NOT STATED, which for a Senior Consultant req should be read with suspicion rather than optimism. Two grades above where a May-2027 graduate enters.
picks.why_fit: It is a Data Product Owner seat on a Customer MDM system — the product-and-analytics hybrid he asked for, and one of very few explicitly product-shaped roles at Deloitte India. Posted "SQL (Mandatory): Advanced capability to query databases, write complex joins, and perform deep-dive analysis to locate data anomalies and investigate data issues" vs SQL (strong) and the CypherSOL work, which was literally anomaly and entity resolution across messy multi-format bank statements. Posted "API Specification & Payload Analysis: Ability to read, interpret, and validate API specs and payloads to troubleshoot integration issues" vs FastAPI across LawzyAI and KOP AI. Posted "Issue Backlog Management" and "Triage & Prioritization: Strong analytical framework to prioritize issues proactively" vs the Bigul product management internship — competitor benchmarking, feature-gap analysis and UX friction mapping on trading and algo workflows is backlog shaping. Posted "Pattern Recognition: Proficiency in analyzing large datasets to identify data quality trends, duplicates, and systemic data patterns" vs the entity-recognition and deduplication work at CypherSOL. Posted "Education: Any Graduate".
picks.gaps: No Master Data Management exposure — no Informatica MDM, no Reltio, no golden-record or survivorship-rule concepts. No enterprise data-lineage or data-governance experience. No experience owning a backlog at enterprise scale or managing stakeholders above a startup founder. And the grade: he is roughly four years short of the Senior Consultant convention, which no certificate fixes.
picks.learnable_edge: SQL window functions, CTEs and query tuning on large tables — 1-2 weeks, free via Mode SQL Tutorial or PostgreSQL Exercises — is what separates "I know SQL" from the posting's "Advanced capability to ... write complex joins, and perform deep-dive analysis", and it is the highest-value single week of study on this entire list because the same bullet recurs across most Deloitte data reqs. A free MDM-concepts primer (2-3 days) at least gives him the vocabulary — golden record, survivorship, match-merge — so he does not sound naive in a screen.
picks.referral_leverage: DECISIVE OR NOTHING. Without a referral the Senior Consultant grade means his CV is never read. With one, the only viable pitch is: the req states Any Graduate and no years, and the team should consider him at Analyst grade against the same scope. He should be prepared for that to be declined. Target Deloitte India AI & Data, AI Insights & Engagement, Bengaluru.
picks.timing: Low priority. Worth ONE conversation, not an application, and specifically the conversation "does this team hire Analysts into the same MDM workstream, and do you take Jan-May final-semester interns?" The team and the subject matter are right for him; the grade is not, and it will not be until roughly 2029.

picks.title: T&T | Cyber - DTP | Sr Analyst | Data Privacy
picks.location: Mumbai, IN — Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP
picks.eligible: Borderline. The years line is the lowest explicit bar of any Mumbai analytics-adjacent role — "Minimum of 1+ years of experience in data protection or privacy compliance" — and his 13 months clears "1+ years" numerically. It does NOT clear "in data protection or privacy compliance", where he has exactly zero.
picks.years_bar: "Minimum of 1+ years of experience in data protection or privacy compliance". The number fits; the domain qualifier does not.
picks.why_fit: Posted "Bachelor's / Master's degree in law, information technology, or a related field" vs B.Tech CSE — cleared. Posted "Minimum of 1+ years" vs ~13 months of internships — cleared on the number alone. Posted "Strong analytical and problem-solving skills" vs 4th of 400+ at Ace The Case IIT Bombay, Spotify case win, IES Business School runner-up, 13 podium finishes. Posted "Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment" vs owning the Infiheal Series A narrative end-to-end at a startup and running 10+ commercial freelance projects solo to Rs 6L+ revenue. The duties include privacy metrics and dashboards, which is the one genuinely analytical thread and where his Power BI and pandas work applies. Mumbai, Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP, Senior Analyst grade.
picks.gaps: The domain, entirely. No data protection work, no privacy compliance work, no DPIA, no RoPA, no data-flow mapping, no DPDPA or GDPR exposure. No CIPT, CIPM or CIPP/E — the posting names all three as preferred and each costs roughly USD 550 plus IAPP membership, which is not a two-week move. Strategically: this is a compliance career, not an analytics one, and it touches only one item on his stated want list (risk analytics) and that only loosely.
picks.learnable_edge: India's DPDP Act 2023 plus GDPR fundamentals — 2 weeks, free, the Act runs about 30 pages and the EDPB publishes free guidance — covers the posting's requirement for knowledge of "regulations, particularly the Personal Data Protection Bill in India" and the DPIA/RoPA vocabulary. That is a genuine 2-week unlock on a Mumbai req. The IAPP certifications are NOT 2-6 week items at that price and he should not commit to one before deciding he wants this career.
picks.referral_leverage: MEDIUM-HIGH on volume. Mumbai Cyber and Data Privacy is where Deloitte India's junior-to-mid Mumbai headcount actually sits — well over 40 Cyber and Data Privacy postings in Mumbai — so alumni density and hiring appetite are both high, and a referral can argue the DPDPA is new enough in India that nobody has deep experience in it yet, which is a true and useful argument. But high leverage into a career he did not ask for is a trap, not an opportunity.
picks.timing: Only if he decides a Mumbai seat at Deloitte India outranks doing analytics. That is a real and defensible choice — Mumbai analytics openings at Deloitte number about two — but he should make it consciously, in writing, before applying. If yes: do the 2-week DPDPA reading, apply by late October 2026, declare June 2027 with a Jan-May 2027 Mumbai internship offer. If no: skip it and put the effort into reqs 112515 and 110231 instead.

skills_to_learn.skill: Microsoft PL-300: Power BI Data Analyst — DAX, Power Query / M, row-level security, tabular semantic models, publishing and scheduling in Power BI Service
skills_to_learn.why: Highest unlock count of anything on this list. It clears FOUR named required skills on req 110508 in one go — "Proficient in making DAX queries in Power BI desktop", "Able to implement row level security on data and have an understanding of application security layer models in Power BI", "Able to develop tabular and multidimensional models that are compatible with warehouse standards", and "Adept in developing, publishing and scheduling Power BI reports" — and req 110508 is the ONLY Power BI requisition on the 2,031-posting India board that lists Mumbai as an eligible location, states no years requirement, and asks only for a B.Tech. It also strengthens req 58184444 ("Proficiency with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Looker)"), req 58386644, and req 59619444 ("Exposure to tools such as Power BI..."). Touches no Java, no C++, no Spark, no warehouse. Roles unlocked or strengthened: 4+.
skills_to_learn.effort: 4-5 weeks part-time. Exam about USD 165 / Rs 4,800. Microsoft Learn PL-300 path is free.
skills_to_learn.resource: Microsoft Learn PL-300 learning path (free) + SQLBI's DAX fundamentals videos (free) + one end-to-end portfolio dashboard built on his own CypherSOL-style transaction data with RLS applied per user

skills_to_learn.why: Named explicitly as the preferred certification on req 110231 — "Relevant certifications (preferred but not mandatory): AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner / Microsoft Azure Fundamentals" — which is one of only two genuinely reachable MUMBAI openings on a 277-posting Mumbai board. It simultaneously clears "Basic understanding of cloud computing and AWS" on req 112515 (the single best-gated role for him anywhere at Deloitte), covers the "Knowledge of cloud security concepts including IAM, networking, encryption, logging, and monitoring" bullet on 110231, and supports "Experience in building applications on cloud platforms like AWS/Azure/GCP" on req 110723. It also converts his AWS Academy ML Foundations from an intro badge into a credential a screener recognises. Roles unlocked or strengthened: 3.
skills_to_learn.effort: 3 weeks part-time. Exam about USD 100 / Rs 8,000.
skills_to_learn.resource: AWS Skill Builder free CLF-C02 Exam Prep course + Stephane Maarek's practice exams

skills_to_learn.skill: ISO 27001:2022 Foundation and NIST CSF 2.0 literacy, plus basic GRC vocabulary (GRC, SOC operations, IAM, BCP/DR)
skills_to_learn.why: Deloitte India's junior Mumbai and Bengaluru hiring volume is overwhelmingly Cyber and Risk — well over 40 Cyber and Data Privacy postings in Mumbai alone — and the same framework bullets recur across all of them at a deliberately low bar. Req 112515 asks only for "Familiarity with ISO 27001 and NIST cybersecurity frameworks" and "Knowledge of GRC, Risk Management, SOC Operations, IAM, and BCP/DR"; req 107779 asks for "Familiarity with NIST CSF 2.0, COBIT, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS"; req 110231 asks for "Familiarity with cloud governance principles and security frameworks". The word in every case is "familiarity" or "basic", not expertise — which is precisely why a short reading effort clears it. Roles unlocked or strengthened: 4 (112515, 110231, 107779, 110382).
skills_to_learn.effort: 2-3 weeks of reading. Free — NIST CSF 2.0 is a free download from NIST; ISO 27001 Annex A control summaries are widely published. Skip the paid Lead Implementer course, it is overkill for a "familiarity" bullet.
skills_to_learn.resource: NIST CSF 2.0 (nist.gov, free) + ISO 27001:2022 Annex A control list walkthrough + any free ISO 27001 Foundation overview course

skills_to_learn.why: Named by name on req 107779 — "Certifications: Possession of (or progress toward) ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC) or similar industry certifications" — and the parenthetical means enrolment alone satisfies the bullet while passing converts it to a hard credential. The CC syllabus also covers the cryptography bullet on the same posting ("Basic understanding of cryptographic concepts (e.g., AES, RSA, hashing, and digital signatures)") and the "Cybersecurity certifications or training" good-to-have on req 112515. It is the single cheapest credential-per-bullet on this list. Roles unlocked or strengthened: 2-3.
skills_to_learn.effort: 2-3 weeks. FREE — course and exam are both free under ISC2's One Million Certified in Cybersecurity programme.
skills_to_learn.resource: ISC2 One Million Certified in Cybersecurity — free self-paced course and free exam voucher at isc2.org

skills_to_learn.skill: Advanced SQL — window functions, CTEs, complex multi-table joins, query tuning on large tables
skills_to_learn.why: SQL appears as a requirement on almost every data role on this board, but the ones that matter ask for a depth above "I write SELECT statements". Req 59240244 asks for "SQL (Mandatory): Advanced capability to query databases, write complex joins, and perform deep-dive analysis to locate data anomalies"; req 59869044 lists "Technical Strength: SQL(Strong)"; req 58184444 says "Proficiency in SQL for data extraction and manipulation is required"; req 112515 lists "Proficiency in Python and SQL". He already has SQL, so this is the cheapest possible upgrade — it makes an existing strength interview-proof rather than building something new. Roles unlocked or strengthened: 4+.
skills_to_learn.resource: Mode Analytics SQL Tutorial (advanced section) + PostgreSQL Exercises + StrataScratch for interview-format problems

skills_to_learn.why: Req 58184444 lists "Tableau, Power BI, Looker" and a strict screener may want the first name rather than accepting the "e.g.". Req 59070444 (the only Mumbai BI Developer opening) says "Ability to query and display large data sets while maximizing the performance of workbook" — "workbook" is Tableau vocabulary, so that req is Tableau in all but name, and although it is out of reach today at 3-5 years, it is his 2028 Mumbai lateral target. Tableau is also the default BI tool at most Indian consulting and analytics employers, so this hedges beyond Deloitte. Rank it AFTER PL-300: doing both is redundant in the short term and PL-300 unlocks more Deloitte reqs. Roles unlocked or strengthened: 2 now, more later.
skills_to_learn.effort: 3 weeks. Exam about USD 100. Tableau Public and the free training videos cost nothing.
skills_to_learn.resource: Tableau eLearning free Desktop Specialist track + Tableau Public portfolio with two dashboards rebuilt from his existing Power BI work

skills_to_learn.skill: India DPDP Act 2023 and GDPR fundamentals — DPIA, RoPA, data-flow mapping, consent and data-principal rights
skills_to_learn.why: Unlocks the highest-volume junior Mumbai practice at Deloitte India. Req 110382 (Mumbai, only "1+ years") requires knowledge of "regulations, particularly the Personal Data Protection Bill in India"; req 111169 requires "Support DPDPA, GDPR, and other data privacy compliance and implementation engagements" and "Assist in conducting Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs), Business Impact Assessments (BIAs), Data Flow Mapping, and Records of Processing Activities (RoPA)". The DPDP Act is new enough in India that nobody has five years of it, which is a genuine levelling opportunity for a fresher. CAVEAT: this unlocks a privacy-compliance career, not an analytics one — only spend the two weeks if he has decided a Mumbai seat outranks doing analytics. Roles unlocked or strengthened: 2 named, plus 40+ Mumbai Cyber and Privacy reqs of the same shape.
skills_to_learn.effort: 2 weeks. Free — the Act is about 30 pages and EDPB/ICO guidance is public. Do NOT buy CIPM or CIPP/E at roughly USD 550 until the career decision is made.
skills_to_learn.resource: DPDP Act 2023 full text (meity.gov.in) + ICO GDPR guide (free) + EDPB DPIA guidelines

skills_to_learn.skill: Salesforce CRM data model and sales data structures
skills_to_learn.why: Narrowest but cheapest unlock on the list. Req 58184444 — the cleanest pure data-analyst JD on the whole board and his second-highest-scoring pick — lists "Experience with CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce) and understanding of sales data structures" as one of only four technical bullets, and it is the ONLY one of the four he currently fails. One failing bullet out of four on an otherwise strong application is worth 10 days to fix.
skills_to_learn.resource: Salesforce Trailhead — "Data Modeling" and "Sales Cloud Basics" trails; free Developer Edition org to poke at the Account/Contact/Opportunity object model directly

referral_strategy:
Referrals matter more at Deloitte India than at almost any employer he will target, for a specific structural reason visible in the data: seven of the ten roles below state NO years requirement at all. When a req is silent on years, the screen is pure discretion — the recruiter falls back on grade convention (Analyst ≈ 0-2, Consultant ≈ 2-4, Senior Consultant ≈ 4+) and CV pedigree. A referral is what gets the CV read before that convention is applied. Conversely, on reqs with an explicit high number (59070444 at 3-5 years, 58524244 at 3-5, 60040244 at 2-6), a referral changes nothing and he should not waste one.

Where to spend referrals, in strict priority order:
1. Requisition 112515 (Analyst | Risk Management | Bengaluru, Cyber Strategy & Transformation). Spend his single best contact here. It is the only posting across 2,745 that says "0-2 years of relevant experience, including internships or academic" — the referrer is not being asked to bend a rule, only to get him read. Quote the requisition number in the message.
2. Requisition 110508 (T&T EAID Power BI, Mumbai listed). Referral is not optional here, it is the whole application — Consultant grade will otherwise sift him out automatically. Ask a Mumbai or Pune T&T EAID contact one direct question: "would the team consider an Analyst-grade hire against 110508, or a Jan-May 2027 final-semester intern?"
3. Requisition 110231 (Senior Analyst, Governance and Policy, MUMBAI). Use a Mumbai-based referrer specifically. This is the strongest candidate for creating a Jan-May 2027 internship, because he is already in Mumbai and costs the team nothing in relocation.

Who to approach, concretely:
- DJSCE TPO first, before any LinkedIn outreach. They know whether Deloitte holds a 2027 slot and whether it is Deloitte India or USI, and they can often make a warmer introduction than a cold alumni message. This is a two-day action with the highest expected value on the entire list.
- DJSCE alumni on LinkedIn, filtered by "Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering" + "Deloitte", then segmented by office: Mumbai for reqs 110231, 110382 and 110508; Bengaluru for 112515, 58184444, 108566 and 107779. Message the requisition number, the two-line availability statement, and one specific line from the posting he matches. Do not send a generic "looking for opportunities" note.
- DJS S4DS network — he was Head of Marketing, which is a legitimate, non-cold reason to contact seniors who graduated into consulting and analytics. Warmer than alumni-search outreach and he has standing to use it.
- Case-competition contacts. Deloitte consultants routinely judge and sponsor campus case competitions. His 4th of 400+ at Ace The Case IIT Bombay, the Spotify case win at KJ Somaiya, the IES Business School runner-up and IIM Ahmedabad Innovability are real openers to anyone from Deloitte who was in those rooms. Check the judging panels and sponsor lists of every competition he placed in — that is a concrete list of names, not a hope.
- Deloitte India campus recruiting. Worth a direct message asking one question only: whether a 2027-batch NLA is planned and when it opens. A dated answer is worth more than five applications.

What NOT to do: do not use a referral on reqs 59070444, 58524244, 60040244, 58605244 or 59668844. The first three carry explicit 3+ or 2-6 year bars, 58605244 is hard-gated on "Education - ACCA Affiliate or ACCA Member", and 59668844 wants 2-4 years of specifically TPRM. Referrals do not override a stated number or a missing professional qualification, and spending one on an impossible req costs him the contact for the possible ones.

One caution the data supports: nothing on either portal speaks to referral mechanics, so the leverage ratings above are inference from Deloitte India's grade conventions and the unusual frequency of no-years-stated reqs, not something I read off a page.
